customers.name: Reptune Transfer Pricing Specialist (Full Service and Collaborative delivery)
customers.description: Works in Reptune's Amsterdam-based specialist team and operates the same Reptune.net platform that clients license, but from the inside: for Full Service clients the specialist coordinates and prepares the whole annual documentation cycle at a fixed rate per Local File, from processing the client's entity financials and transactional data through drafting, benchmark and agreement insertion, localisation and translation to delivered Master File and Local Files; for Collaborative clients the work is split with the client's transfer pricing manager and local finance contacts. Typically joins from a Big 4 or in-house transfer pricing role, handles a portfolio of multinationals with 5 to 100+ entities each, and prepares documentation in about 25 percent of the time a traditional adviser needs because the client's model, templates and country rules are already configured. Also spends the 2, 4 or 8 expert hours included per plan on on-demand advice, functional analysis questions and audit support, and hands work back and forth when a client switches between On Demand, Collaborative and Full Service. Is judged on Local Files delivered per year, delivery lead time, rework and the margin on fixed-fee engagements.
careAbout: A client transfer pricing model that is complete and consistent before the season starts, because every gap in entities, transactions, functional analyses or benchmarks becomes a manual fix multiplied across Local Files
Client data arriving validated and on time through Excel templates or the ERP integration, rather than as a trickle of e-mails that has to be reconciled by hand under deadline pressure
Generating a full batch of Local Files in one run and spending specialist time on judgement, custom text and local nuance rather than on formatting and copying
Localised templates, deadlines and language rules for each country that are already correct in the platform so the specialist does not have to research every jurisdiction anew
The client seeing progress, open questions and delivered files in the same workflow the specialist works in, so status calls and reminder e-mails disappear
Delivering each Local File within the fixed rate and the planned hours, because overruns on a fixed-fee engagement come straight out of Reptune's margin
winsThem: A full-service delivery workspace that shows every client, entity, Local File, task, open data request and expert hour in one queue, so a specialist runs ten clients as easily as one
Rule-based generation from a configured model, so a batch of Local Files for 40 countries is produced and validated in a day and only exceptions need a specialist's eye

Country regulations, localised templates and auto-calculated deadlines maintained by the content team, so the specialist trusts the platform to know Italy, Germany and Brazil better than a generic template
Machine translation into 28 languages with transfer pricing glossaries, plus human-certified translation on request, so localisation is a review step instead of a subcontracting project
A service-level neutral setup: the same model, workflow and files serve On Demand, Collaborative and Full Service, so switching a client's service level is a task reassignment rather than a migration
theirFear: Discovering during the peak season that a client's transactional data or functional analyses were incomplete and having to redo dozens of Local Files by hand at a fixed fee
A Local File that fails a local audit because a country requirement changed and the specialist relied on last year's template
A client escalating to the CEO because a status question went unanswered in a mailbox while the work was in fact on track

jobsToBeDone.name: Deliver complete, compliant documentation for a client at a fixed fee and margin
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Run a Full Service or Collaborative client's annual documentation cycle end-to-end on the platform: take over or set up the client's transfer pricing model, scope entities and countries, process the client's data, generate and review Master File and Local Files, localise and translate them, and deliver final documents before every deadline, all within the fixed rate per Local File and the specialist hours planned for the engagement.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Every scoped Master File and Local File for the client is delivered complete, validated and locally compliant before its deadline, at a quarter of the hours a traditional adviser would spend, with the fixed-fee engagement closed inside its planned margin and no rework caused by Reptune.

steps.step: Take over or set up the client's transfer pricing model
steps.description: Review the client's entities, intercompany transactions, company types, functional analyses, transfer pricing methods and benchmarks in the platform, or configure them from the client's policy documents, agreements and prior-year reports when a new Full Service client comes on board. Fill gaps once in the model rather than later in individual files, and load the client's corporate identity and template preferences so generated reports need no post-editing.

streamsNeeded.name: Set Up the Transfer Pricing Model
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the structured model of entities, transactions, functional analyses, methods, benchmarks and templates that the specialist configures once, with Excel bulk entry and the R-AI onboarding assistant to go live in days.

streamsNeeded.name: Deliver Documentation as a Service
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Records the engagement, its service level and fixed rate per Local File and gives the specialist the delivery workspace in which the model take-over is tracked as the first milestone.

steps.step: Scope the cycle and agree the delivery plan with the client
steps.description: Decide with the client which entities need a Local File, which countries require a Master File, CbCR or notification, and which thresholds exempt small entities; let the platform calculate the deadlines per country and lay them out as a delivery plan with data request dates, drafting windows, client review rounds and translation lead times. Assign tasks between the specialist, client contacts and local advisers according to the service level.

streamsNeeded.name: Scope and Plan the Annual Documentation Cycle
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Turns the fiscal year and entity list into scoped documentation per entity and country with auto-calculated deadlines, assigned tasks, e-mail reminders and a compliance dashboard the client and specialist share.

streamsNeeded.name: Maintain Country Regulations and Deadlines
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Supplies the thresholds, content requirements and deadline rules per country that determine which entities are in scope and when each file must be ready.

streamsNeeded.name: Deliver Documentation as a Service
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Holds the delivery plan, planned specialist hours per Local File and the client-visible milestones for the engagement.

steps.step: Process the client's financial and transactional data
steps.description: Send the client's finance contacts the Excel templates or trigger the ERP extract, load entity financials, segmented P&L and transactional volumes, run the validations and chase the actions required before generation. For Collaborative clients, review what the client has entered; for Full Service clients, do the segmentation and reconciliations on their behalf.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Financial and Transactional Data
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the Excel templates, bulk upload, validation rules and the actions-required list that show the specialist exactly which entity data is missing or inconsistent.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate with ERP, Operational TP and Identity
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Pulls financials and transactional data directly from the client's ERP or operational transfer pricing solution where an integration exists, removing the manual data round trip.

steps.step: Generate, draft and review Master File and Local Files
steps.description: Generate the full batch of Local Files and the Master File from the validated model, insert benchmarks and intercompany agreements from the archive, write the custom text for restructurings, loss-making entities or unusual transactions with AI-assisted writing, compare segmented results against the arm's-length ranges, and put every file through a second-specialist review before it goes to the client.

streamsNeeded.name: Generate Master File and Local Files
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Produces draft and final Master File and Local Files at the press of a button with template selection, benchmark and agreement insertion, custom text and report styling.

streamsNeeded.name: Benchmark Intercompany Transactions
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Supplies the archived benchmark studies and arm's-length ranges and flags entities whose segmented results fall outside their range so the specialist can address them in the file.

streamsNeeded.name: Manage Legal Entities and Intercompany Agreements
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the signed intercompany agreements and time-stamped entity data that are inserted into the documentation as evidence.

steps.step: Localise, translate and deliver the final files
steps.description: Apply the localised template, content rules and local forms for each country, run machine translation with the transfer pricing glossary and order human-certified translation where the tax authority requires it, review the local version with the client's country contact, and deliver the final file with filing guidance before the deadline, archived with its version history.

streamsNeeded.name: Localise and Translate Documentation
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Turns the English Local File into a locally compliant, translated file with country templates, glossaries, machine or human-certified translation and local forms and procedures.

streamsNeeded.name: Deliver Documentation as a Service
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Tracks delivery of each final file against the engagement plan, records the hours spent per Local File and closes the milestone visibly for the client.

streamsNeeded.name: Monitor Compliance and Defend Audits

streamsNeeded.name: Scope and Plan the Annual Documentation Cycle

streamsNeeded.name: Monitor Compliance and Defend Audits

streamsNeeded.name: Deliver Documentation as a Service
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Tracks included and additional expert hours per client and engagement so advice is visible to the client and billable beyond the plan.

jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Let a client step up from On Demand or Collaborative to Full Service when its tax team is stretched, or step down when it has built its own capacity, without re-implementing the model, re-collecting data or re-drafting files, because the specialist has kept the client's setup, workflow and documents service-level neutral on the same platform.

customerJourneyStories.name: From Big 4 documentation projects to platform-based delivery
customerJourneyStories.summary: A transfer pricing senior who joins Reptune from a Big 4 practice adopts Reptune.net and the full-service ways of working, from the first onboarding week and a sceptical look at the rule-based generator to running a portfolio of Full Service clients at a quarter of the hours she used to bill.

stages.narrative: After six years of preparing Local Files in Word and Excel for a Big 4 practice, the specialist joins Reptune as the team grows beyond its 20 members under Vortex. In her first week she is assigned a portfolio of Full Service clients with more than 200 Local Files between them and a fixed rate per file, and realises that her old way of working, billing hours per document, would make the engagements loss-making.

The onboarding programme puts her in front of the platform on day one: she works through the R-AI onboarding assistant, shadows a senior specialist running a client's cycle in the delivery workspace, and sees the dashboard, workflow, generator, country regulations and translation module the clients themselves use. The senior shows how a batch of 40 Local Files was generated from a configured model in a single afternoon.

She is sceptical that generated documentation can hold up in an audit and tests the platform on a case she knows: a loss-making distributor in Italy. She checks the localised Italian template against the requirements she remembers, runs the pre-generation validation and sees that it catches the missing benchmark she deliberately left out, and reads the testimonials from customers whose files held in audits. What convinces her is that the custom text field and AI-assisted writing leave the judgement to her while the structure and consistency come from the model.

Her first real engagement is a Collaborative client with twelve entities: she takes over the model review and generation while the client's transfer pricing manager collects the data, and a senior reviews every file before delivery. The batch is delivered three weeks before the earliest deadline, her hours per Local File come in at a fraction of her Big 4 benchmark, and the client's only comments are on custom text, not on structure or numbers.

Within a quarter she runs her full portfolio of Full Service clients from the delivery workspace: scoping and deadlines per country come from the platform, data requests go out as assigned tasks with reminders, generation and localisation are batch jobs, and she spends her time on functional analyses, restructurings, audit questions and the client's expert hours. Her clients watch progress on the same dashboard she works in, so status e-mails have disappeared.

A year in she reviews other specialists' files, contributes template and validation improvements to the content team, and is the named contact when a Collaborative client steps up to Full Service. She stays because the platform gives her leverage and the interesting work: the documentation that used to fill her year is now a quarter of it, and the rest is advice clients actually pay for.

customerJourneyStories.name: Moving client delivery from mailboxes into the full-service delivery workspace
customerJourneyStories.summary: The specialist team adopts the in-platform full-service delivery workspace, replacing the mailboxes, shared drives and hour sheets it used to coordinate client engagements, and ends up with client-visible progress, tracked expert hours and service-level switches that no longer require a hand-over project.

stages.narrative: A Full Service client's head of tax escalates because a status question sat unanswered in a specialist's mailbox during holidays while the work was in fact on track, and in the same month the team discovers that expert hours for two clients were undercounted because they lived in personal spreadsheets. The team lead concludes that coordinating engagements outside the platform the clients already use is the problem.

The product team demonstrates the full-service delivery workspace it has built on top of the workflow: every engagement with its service level, fixed rate per Local File, delivery plan, assigned tasks, review rounds and expert hours in one queue, with the client seeing the same milestones on its dashboard. The specialists recognise their own way of working, only without the mailbox.

The team debates whether client-visible progress exposes half-finished drafts and internal notes, and whether logging hours per Local File will be used against them. Access rights that keep internal review comments and time entries out of the client's view, and a margin report that shows overruns per engagement rather than per person, settle the discussion; the ISO 27001 controls mean no new security review is needed.

Two clients, one Full Service and one Collaborative, are run in the workspace for a cycle. The clients answer data requests faster because tasks arrive as reminders with a deadline, the specialists stop writing weekly status e-mails, and the hours per Local File become visible per engagement for the first time.

All engagements move into the workspace at the start of the next season. The team lead plans capacity from the queue and the deadlines per country, specialists pick up each other's clients during holidays because everything is in one place, and the expert hours per client are reviewed monthly with sales to spot advisory demand beyond the plan.

When a Collaborative client steps up to Full Service mid-cycle, the switch is a reassignment of the open tasks and a repriced engagement in the workspace instead of a hand-over project, and the client notices nothing but more done. The workspace becomes the place where the team's fixed-fee margin is managed, and no specialist wants to go back to mailboxes.

customers.name: Country Regulations and Content Specialist
customers.description: A transfer pricing specialist in Reptune's localisation and country content team who keeps the platform's knowledge of more than 170 countries current: for each jurisdiction the documentation thresholds, Master File and Local File content requirements, filing formats, language and translation requirements, local forms and procedures, and the deadline rules for Master File, Local Files, CbCR and CbCR notifications from which the platform calculates every entity's deadlines. Maintains the OECD-aligned standard templates and the localised templates such as the Italian one, the transfer pricing glossaries behind machine translation into 28 languages, and the knowledge base that R-AI's coming Local Requirements country-expert mode answers from. Follows OECD, EU (including Directive 2021/2101 on public CbCR) and local legislative changes, works with local advisers where Reptune has no presence, and answers country-expert queries from Reptune's own specialists, advisers and clients. Is judged on how current and correct the country rule sets are, how fast regulatory changes reach the platform, and how quickly and reliably country questions are resolved.
careAbout: A structured rule model per country in which thresholds, content, format, language and deadline rules are data the platform acts on, not prose that someone has to read and interpret each season
Learning about a regulatory change within days of its publication in any of 170+ countries, including those where Reptune relies on local advisers and official sources in the local language
Deadlines that auto-calculate correctly for every entity in every country, because a wrong deadline rule multiplies into missed filings across 150+ client groups
Localised templates, local forms and translation glossaries that make the generated file locally acceptable without the specialist or client re-researching the country
Country-expert queries answered once and reused, so the same question about Brazilian formats or Polish thresholds is not answered by e-mail twenty times a season
Knowing that every rule change was reviewed by a second specialist and versioned, so the team can show a client when and why a country rule changed
winsThem: A country regulations back office in which each rule has a source, an effective date, a reviewer and a version, and in which a change flows straight into scoping, deadline calculation, validation and the dashboard
Change monitoring across official sources, adviser networks and OECD and EU publications that lands as review tasks per country instead of a reading list
Template and validation tooling that lets a content specialist adjust a localised template or add a pre-generation check without a software release
Glossary management per language that keeps machine translation consistent for transfer pricing terms and feeds the human-certified translation partners
A curated knowledge base behind R-AI Local Requirements, so routine country questions are answered by the assistant in any language and the specialist handles only the hard ones

jobsToBeDone.name: Keep 170+ country rule sets and deadlines current and correct
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Maintain, for every country the platform supports, the current thresholds, documentation content and format requirements, language requirements, CbCR and notification obligations and deadline rules, detecting regulatory change quickly, encoding it as structured rules with sources and effective dates, and releasing it through review so that scoping, deadline calculation, validation and the dashboard reflect the law as it stands.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Every country rule set is verified current within its review cycle, regulatory changes reach the platform within days rather than the next season, deadlines calculate correctly for every entity, and no client or specialist relies on a rule that has been superseded.

steps.step: Monitor regulatory change per country
steps.description: Follow OECD BEPS Action 13 guidance, EU directives, national legislation, tax authority guidance and adviser network alerts for each country, including public CbCR under Directive 2021/2101 and Pillar Two safe-harbour interactions, and log each relevant change as a review task on the country it concerns with its source and expected effective date.

steps.description: Define per country how the deadlines for Master File, Local Files, CbCR and CbCR notifications derive from fiscal year end, tax return dates, submission on request periods and extensions, test the rule against sample entities with different year ends, and release it so the workflow and dashboard show the correct date for every entity.

jobsToBeDone.outcome: A user in any country generates a file that already reflects the current local requirement, is warned about gaps before generation, gets consistent translations, and receives a correct country answer within hours, from R-AI for routine questions and from a specialist for the hard ones, with the answer reused the next time it is asked.

customerJourneyStories.name: From country spreadsheets to the in-platform regulation base
customerJourneyStories.summary: The content team adopts the platform's country regulations back office, moving 170+ country rule sets out of shared spreadsheets and Word notes into structured, versioned rules that drive scoping, deadlines, validation and templates, and ends up as the curated source behind R-AI's country-expert answers.

stages.narrative: A change to a country's Local File deadline is recorded in the team's country spreadsheet but not in the platform's deadline settings, and a client's dashboard shows the old date until a local adviser flags it three weeks before filing. The post-mortem finds four places where country knowledge lives, none of them the platform, and a team that has grown with the client base beyond what spreadsheets can hold.

The product team walks the content specialists through the country regulations back office it has been building: one rule set per country with thresholds, content, format, language and deadline rules as data, each with source, effective date, reviewer and version, and each feeding scoping, deadline calculation, validation and the dashboard directly. The specialists see their spreadsheet columns as rule types and their Word notes as knowledge entries.

The team's concern is nuance: many country requirements are conditional or interpreted differently by tax authorities and do not fit a fixed schema. They evaluate the rule model on the hardest cases they know, including thresholds that depend on group revenue and transaction type and deadlines that hang on tax return dates with extensions, and agree once conditional rules, free-text guidance and a review gate before release are supported. Version history that can show what applied in a prior year settles the audit-defence argument.

Ten countries with the most client entities are migrated first, each rule cross-checked by a second specialist against its source. A parallel run for one season shows the auto-calculated deadlines match the spreadsheet where the spreadsheet was right and differ where it was stale, and the first regulatory change of the season is released through the back office in three days instead of waiting for the next spreadsheet round.

All 170+ countries are in the back office within two quarters. Change monitoring lands as review tasks per country, releases go out weekly with reviewer and effective date, localised templates and validation rules are edited by the content team without a software release, and clients see a rule change on their dashboard the day it is released.

The regulation base becomes the platform's second strategic asset: the R-AI Local Requirements mode is built on its entries, sales cites countries covered and update lead time in every proposal, and the content team measures itself on coverage currency and update lead time instead of on how many e-mails it answered. No one would go back to a spreadsheet.

customerJourneyStories.name: Becoming the specialists behind R-AI's country-expert answers
customerJourneyStories.summary: A content specialist adopts the knowledge-base curation workflow behind R-AI's Local Requirements mode, from doubt that an assistant should answer country questions at all to a routine in which R-AI resolves the routine queries in any language and the specialist curates entries and handles the hard ones.

stages.narrative: With more than 150 client groups and a growing adviser channel, the content team's mailbox receives the same country questions dozens of times a season, in several languages, and query response times stretch to days in the peak. The team lead is asked how country expertise can scale without hiring a specialist for every ten new clients.

The AI team presents the plan for R-AI Local Requirements: the existing R-AI assistant, which already answers onboarding and product questions in any language, extended with a country-expert mode that answers from curated knowledge entries linked to the regulation base. The specialist sees a draft answer about Italian documentation requirements generated from her own entries, in Italian.

The specialist's objection is liability: a confident wrong answer about a threshold or deadline is worse than a slow correct one. She evaluates the curation controls: every entry linked to a rule and source, automatic stale-marking when the underlying rule changes, answers that cite the entry and its effective date, escalation to a specialist for questions outside the curated entries, and a monthly sample review of answers per language. The team agrees to pilot with those gates in place.

Fifteen countries with the highest query volume are curated first and the country-expert mode is opened to Reptune's own specialists before clients. Within a month the assistant resolves most of the routine questions for those countries, the specialist reviews a sample of answers every week, and two entries are corrected before any client sees them.

Curation becomes part of every rule release: when a country rule changes, the specialist updates the knowledge entries in the same workflow, marks the old ones stale and checks the assistant's answer before release. Clients on the Advanced and Enterprise plans and advisers use the country-expert mode in their own languages, and the specialist's queue holds only the questions that need judgement or a local adviser.

Query resolution time and coverage currency improve season after season, the R-AI Country Expert add-on becomes one of the reasons clients upgrade, and the specialist's expertise is visible in every answer the assistant gives. She stays because the work has moved from answering the same question twenty times to deciding what the right answer is for 170+ countries.
